To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

two classes of micro filaments, tropomyosin-rich microfilaments and alpha- actinin-rich microfilaments, were isolated from chicken embryo cells by monoclonal antibody affinity chromatography, and that these two classes of microfi laments differ in their protein composition, in their ability to activate myosin Mg2+-AT Pase, and in their ultrastructure.
tropomyosin and alpha-actinins, two microfilament-associated regulatory proteins, can be isolated from microfilaments by monoclonal antibody affinity column.

tropomyosin and alpha-actin are two distinct classes of microfilament proteins which are differentially assembled into two classes of micro- filaments, and the assembly of these two classes of microfi- laments is coordinately regulated by actin polymerization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the microfilament proteins which are responsible for the regulation of microfilament assembly and function.
the isolation, characterization, and regulation of microfilament assembly of chicken embryo fibroblast.
the isolation of two types of microfilaments from chicken embryo fibrobasts by the use of monoclonal antibodies and with the characterization of their biochemical and morphological properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two types of microfilaments isolated here were different in their composition, morphology, and function and that they may be the two major classes of microfilament in cultured fibroblasts, which may be involved in different functions in the cell.
tropomyosin is the major component of microfilaments in chicken embryo fibroblast cells, while alpha- actinin, a microfilament-associated protein, is a minor component of the microfilaments.
the microfilament system is a complex structure and that the assembly of the microfilament-associated components is a coordinated process.

the two classes of micro- filaments are not identical in terms of their composition or function, and that the microfilament assembly is regulated in a complex manner.
